interest: Shows 1940-41 U.S. firms squeezed by Japanese controls and freezing orders, plus FBI surveillance and wartime zaibatsu shipping intelligence.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.5034, covering corporations, capital, and business regulations in Japan from 1940 to 1944) documents the squeeze on American corporate investments in Japan preceding the outbreak of the Pacific War and Allied wartime intelligence on Japanese corporate reorganizations. In early 1941, Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reported that Japanese industrial mobilization laws and exchange controls threatened American manufacturers (including Ford, General Motors, and Otis Elevator) with expropriation, leading to internal State Department debate over retaliatory liquidation of Japanese assets in the United States. Subsequent documents from late summer and autumn 1941 detail Japanese employee severance demands on American businesses under threat of exit permit denials, corporate restructuring inquiries (Hanson-Van Winkle-Munning Co. and American Express), and FBI reports on Japanese firms destroying records in New York amid rumors of war. The later section contains wartime reports from 1943 and 1944 via Buenos Aires and Stockholm regarding the establishment of Mitsui Shipping Company and the operations of Nippon Yusen Kaisha under the state Ship-control Corporation, alongside a 1940 memorandum analyzing Japanese wartime labor shortages and statistical sources.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew warns of newly enacted Japanese industrial control legislation squeezing out American manufacturing corporations and recommends reciprocal liquidation controls over Japanese assets in the United States.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan (Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 383: Grew reports Japan's new industrial controls—licensing, expropriation, price fixing, mandatory Japanese board and share majorities—threaten Ford, GM, and Otis Elevator with exclusion; after three fruitless years of protest, Grew recommends the U.S. mirror its treatment of Japanese holdings.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 383 (Sections 1 and 2) from Ambassador Grew on Japanese Industrial Controls over American Corporations

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum analyzing Ambassador Grew's proposal for reciprocal liquidation of Japanese assets in the United States.
subfiles.from: Frederick Livesey, Office of the Adviser on International Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Livesey assesses Grew's retaliation proposal: Japan's licensing rules resemble unimplemented British wartime measures; liquidating Japanese assets to pay American claimants risks economic isolationism and legal difficulties, though an inventory could be done under existing law.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Frederick Livesey on Ambassador Grew's Proposed Retaliatory Liquidation of Japanese Assets
subfiles.to: J. Weis (routed to Assistant Secretary Dean Acheson)

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports exorbitant severance demands made by Japanese employees of American firms backed by the withholding of exit permits by Japanese authorities.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan (Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 1194: Grew reports Japanese employees at American firms, anticipating shutdowns, demand one-two months' pay per year of service, three months' notice, and in one case a 30% raise and 55% share transfer; Japan is denying exit permits until demands are met.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1194 from Ambassador Grew on Japanese Employee Demands and Departure Restrictions

subfiles.about: Paraphrase of Ambassador Grew's confidential telegram reporting employee retirement demands and departure permit denials facing American firms in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of Telegram 1194: Japanese employees demand retirement allowances of one-two months' pay per service year and three months' notice, with one firm facing a 30% wage hike and 55% share transfer demand; Japanese officials back these by denying Americans exit permits until staff are satisfied.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 1194 from Tokyo on Employee Demands and Exit Denials

subfiles.about: Attorney William J. Sebald inquires whether Japanese law requires corporate officers to be Japanese nationals or restricts foreign corporate share ownership.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, Attorney at Law
subfiles.summary: Attorney Sebald reports that Hanson-Van Winkle-Munning's Kobe subsidiary is paralyzed by Japanese freezing orders while incurring wage costs, and advisors suggested replacing American directors and auditors with Japanese nationals; he asks whether Japan requires Japanese corporate officers or bars foreign shareholding control.
subfiles.title: Letter from William J. Sebald Regarding K.K. A.P. Munning & Co. and Japanese Corporate Nationality Requirements
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover reports intelligence that Japanese firms in New York City were instructed to destroy documents and rumors that Japan expected war by August 20, 1941.
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports to Berle that Japanese firms in New York were liquidating on consular orders to destroy documents, amid persistent rumors in Japanese circles that Japan expected war with the U.S. by August 20, 1941; copies went to ONI and Army G-2.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. Edgar Hoover to Adolf A. Berle, Jr. on Japanese Firm Document Destruction and War Rumors
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: State Department internal charge slip recording loans of enclosure items from pre-war files in late 1946 and early 1947.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Charge slip tracks records borrowed from file 760D.61: enclosure 1347 to Gates (Nov. 1946) and item 26 to Pratt (Jan. 1947).
subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip for File 760D.61

subfiles.about: Archival confidential file separation sheet marking the classified storage of document 894.5034/26.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: Separation sheet shows document 894.5034/26 (Hoover's FBI report to Berle) was segregated into the State Department's Confidential File.
subfiles.title: Confidential File Separation Sheet for Decimal File 894.5034/26

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs the Tokyo Embassy to report whether Japan has promulgated regulations barring foreign corporate officers or foreign share ownership.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 563 asks the Tokyo Embassy, prompted by Sebald's inquiry on Hanson-Van Winkle-Munning, whether Japan requires foreign-controlled firms' officers to be Japanese subjects or bars foreign share control.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 563 to American Embassy Tokyo Regarding Japanese Corporate Governance Regulations

subfiles.about: Attorney M. John Silver inquires about the corporate identity and incorporation status of the American Express business in Yokohama.
subfiles.from: M. John Silver, Attorney at Law
subfiles.summary: Attorney M. John Silver asks the State Department whether American Express's Yokohama travelers-cheque and banking business operates as American Express Company or American Express Company, Inc., and whether it is formally incorporated.
subfiles.title: Letter from M. John Silver Inquiring on American Express Corporate Status in Yokohama

subfiles.about: The Department of State advises M. John Silver that the Yokohama office of American Express is operated under the incorporated name American Express Company, Inc.
subfiles.from: George Atcheson, Jr., Assistant Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: George Atcheson, Jr. replies to Silver that American Express confirmed its Yokohama branch operates as 'American Express Company, Inc.' and is fully incorporated, referring him to the company's New York headquarters.
subfiles.title: Letter from George Atcheson, Jr. to M. John Silver Regarding American Express Branch in Yokohama
subfiles.to: M. John Silver, Attorney at Law

subfiles.about: American Express agrees to maintain its Yokohama service office until late November 1941 to assist the Department of State.
subfiles.from: Ralph T. Reed, Vice President, The American Express Company, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Ralph T. Reed of American Express tells George L. Brandt that the company cabled its Manila manager to keep the Yokohama service unit open until the end of November 1941, to assist Americans withdrawing from Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ralph T. Reed to George L. Brandt on Maintaining American Express Office in Yokohama
subfiles.to: George L. Brandt, Chief, Special Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing IBM correspondence regarding royalty difficulties and business operations of its Japanese subsidiary, Watson Business Machine Japan, Ltd.
subfiles.from: International Business Machines Corporation (J. A. Phillips)
subfiles.summary: Indexes an IBM letter on difficulties securing royalties and protecting assets of its Japanese subsidiary, Watson Business Machine Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Protection of IBM and Watson Business Machine Japan, Ltd.

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting Domei press releases announcing the spin-off and establishment of Mitsui Shipping Company Ltd. (Mitsui Sempaku K.K.) and its Argentine agent.
subfiles.from: Richard Ford, First Secretary of Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 8033: Buenos Aires reports via Domei that Mitsui Bussan's shipping arm became an independent company, Mitsui Sempaku (Mitsui Shipping Company Ltd.), capitalized at 50,000,000 yen, with Mitsui's Argentine business run by Nambei Trading under Isoma Kobayashi.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 8033 from Embassy Buenos Aires on the Establishment of Mitsui Shipping Company Ltd.

subfiles.about: Despatch forwarding a translation of a German occupation press report on the wartime expansion, management reforms, and profits of Nippon Yusen Kaisha.
subfiles.from: Herschel V. Johnson, U.S. Minister to Sweden (Stockholm)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 2891: Stockholm forwards a German-occupation press article reporting NYK's wartime success after Japan's Ship-control Corporation centralized merchant shipping under its management, including an 8% dividend, reserve growth, and successful wooden cargo-vessel construction.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2891 from Legation Stockholm Enclosing Press Report on Nippon Yusen Kaisha

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum analyzing Tokyo Embassy Despatch 4713 regarding Japanese labor shortages, wage-price trends, and statistical sources.
subfiles.from: Ivan B. White, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: White reviews a Tokyo Embassy report on Japan's labor shortages, falling real wages, and the banned Abe-faction labor party, disputing the claim that labor statistics were suppressed by listing published wage, price, and living-cost series from the Bank of Japan, government bureaus, Asahi Shimbun, and Chambers of Commerce.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Ivan B. White on Japanese Labor Problems and Available Economic Statistics
